assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Removing the isinstance(_transient_transport_errors()) test at imas_codex/discovery/base/llm.py:2629 gives each parametrised fault one attempt, so fake.call_count reads 1 instead of 3; base-arm.log records exactly that failure for both httpx.ConnectError and httpx.ReadError.

Widening the type test at llm.py:2629 to Exception makes call_count 3 instead of 1 for the deterministic ValueError, so this assertion reddens; it passes at base as well, so it guards against a future widening rather than evidencing this change.
Removing the per-candidate catch entirely at worker_compose_batches.py:612 propagates the ValidationError and no refusal is recorded, so refusals is empty and the source_id/reason assertions redden.

Restoring the bare Exception catch at worker_compose_batches.py:612 absorbs the AttributeError, so pytest.raises does not fire and refusals/persisted are both non-empty; negative-control.log records exactly this single failure.

findings.text: non-blocking: the done-when's second half — that one transport fault costs at most the LLM loop's max_retries attempts at the compose seam — is guarded only at the LLM layer. No test in tests/standard_names/test_compose_batch_isolation.py asserts how many times compose_batch calls acall_llm_structured for one attempt, and the test that did pin this seam (the old calls == 2 assertion) was deleted with the wrapper. Re-adding a retry wrapper around this call would redden no test, so the regression the node exists to remove could return unnoticed.

non-blocking: the comment and the evidence fragment claim the fault set is read from its owner rather than restated, but nothing pins that property. Replacing _transient_transport_errors() at line 2630 with a hardcoded (httpx.ConnectError, httpx.ReadError) leaves tests/discovery/test_llm_transport_retry.py green, because both parametrised faults are exactly those two types. The deleted test_the_retry_set_is_read_from_the_llm_layer was the only guard on it, and its replacement tests the loop's count rather than where the set comes from.
